dimensions.name: Discoverability & AEO Readiness
dimensions.summary: Whether answer engines and shoppers can find, read and trust the retailer's product pages.

dimensions.name: Data & Content Foundation
dimensions.summary: Whether product, price, stock and policy data is structured, complete and joined up.

dimensions.name: AI & Agent Adoption
dimensions.summary: Whether AI assistants and agentic workflows are live for customers or colleagues.

dimensions.name: Operating Model & Measurement
dimensions.summary: Whether AI has named owners, training, and measured outcomes. Merges the former D4 and D5.

levels.name: Ad hoc
levels.meaning: A confirmed basic or isolated practice with limited repeatability
levels.min_evidence: Positive evidence of the practice and its limited scope. Silence never qualifies.

levels.name: Defined
levels.meaning: An identifiable capability, initiative or owner
levels.min_evidence: A concrete scope and a traceable description or observable example.

levels.name: Operational
levels.meaning: A live workflow or repeatable operating capability
levels.min_evidence: Evidence of use in a stated scope. A future rollout announcement is insufficient.

levels.name: Managed
levels.meaning: A scaled capability with controls and measured performance
levels.min_evidence: Operating and outcome evidence across more than one cycle, plus named accountability.

levels.name: Adaptive
levels.meaning: Continuous improvement and sustained value across the agreed scope
levels.min_evidence: Repeated learning, governed changes and durable outcomes. A vendor claim of leadership is insufficient.

cells.name: Ad hoc
cells.test: Basic product information exists and discoverability gaps are documented
cells.threshold: ≥5 sampled product pages found for the market; ≥1 gap logged
cells.requirement: Product pages exist and are findable in the market, with discoverability gaps noted
cells.anchor: Basic product information exists, with documented gaps in consistency or discoverability.
cells.evidence: Dated examples of pages and a recorded search or content issue.
cells.boundary: Missing schema or low AI visibility cannot be inferred without testing.

cells.name: Defined
cells.test: Defined product-content or search capability supports selection
cells.threshold: ≥80% of sampled pages carry structured specs; site search or compare tool is live
cells.requirement: Structured product content, search, filters and comparison support product selection
cells.anchor: A defined product-content or search capability supports product selection.
cells.evidence: An observable category, product comparison, search feature or documented discovery initiative.
cells.boundary: A structured-looking page does not prove machine-readable content quality.

cells.name: Operational
cells.test: Live AI / conversational discovery operates in the stated market
cells.threshold: Live AI discovery surface observed in the stated market, or stated by a primary retailer source
cells.requirement: AI or conversational discovery live in the market, confirmed by observation or a primary source
cells.anchor: A live AI discovery or conversational shopping route serves a stated market or assortment.
cells.evidence: A current journey observation, or an explicit live retailer account pending validation.
cells.boundary: A launch plan, generic AI marketing or standard keyword search does not meet this level.

cells.name: Managed
cells.test: A repeatable visibility & accuracy audit drives remediation
cells.threshold: Audit repeated ≥2 cycles; ≥80% answer accuracy; named owner and a fix log
cells.requirement: Visibility and accuracy audited on a repeat cycle, with a named owner and a record of fixes
cells.anchor: A repeatable visibility and accuracy audit informs remediation across the agreed assortment.
cells.evidence: Question-set results across at least two review cycles, an owner and evidence of corrective action.
cells.boundary: A one-time traffic spike does not prove managed discovery.

cells.name: Adaptive
cells.test: Continuous, controlled improvement with sustained commercial outcomes
cells.threshold: ≥3 improvement cycles; ≥90% accuracy sustained; uplift vs a control group
cells.requirement: Continuous improvement, accuracy sustained, and commercial uplift shown against a control
cells.anchor: The retailer continuously improves discovery using controlled learning and sustained commercial outcomes.
cells.evidence: Multiple improvement cycles, stable measurement and evidence linking changes to incremental results.
cells.boundary: Visibility leadership claims and citation counts alone are insufficient.

cells.name: Ad hoc
cells.test: Basic product records exist, possibly with manual or inconsistent handling
cells.threshold: Source records found for sampled SKUs; inconsistencies logged
cells.requirement: Product records exist for sampled SKUs, with inconsistencies noted
cells.anchor: The scoped journey uses basic records with documented manual or inconsistent handling.
cells.evidence: A source record, workflow description and specific inconsistency.
cells.boundary: Do not infer fragmentation from the absence of a public data strategy.

cells.name: Defined
cells.test: Defined attributes / content structures cover a product scope
cells.threshold: ≥80% of sampled SKUs carry required fields (ID, specs, price, terms)
cells.requirement: Required fields (ID, specs, price, terms) present across a defined product scope
cells.anchor: Defined attributes or content structures support an identifiable product or offer scope.
cells.evidence: Representative product fields, category attributes or a documented common content standard.
cells.boundary: One example supports the scoped capability only.

cells.name: Operational
cells.test: A live workflow combines multiple data types
cells.threshold: ≥1 live workflow joins ≥2 data types (product + stock, support or order)
cells.requirement: A live workflow combines two or more data types, e.g. product with stock, order or support
cells.anchor: A live workflow combines multiple relevant data types to serve customers or colleagues.
cells.evidence: Evidence linking product information with inventory, support, account or transaction data.
cells.boundary: A planned migration or future integration does not establish live use.

cells.name: Managed
cells.test: Owners manage data quality and freshness against targets
cells.threshold: Owned quality KPIs; ≥95% field accuracy held over ≥2 cycles
cells.requirement: Data quality and freshness managed to owned KPIs over two or more cycles, with an incident log
cells.anchor: Owners manage data quality and freshness against defined service targets.
cells.evidence: Quality metrics, incident records, accountable owners and performance over at least two cycles.
cells.boundary: An API or data platform alone does not establish quality management.

cells.name: Adaptive
cells.test: Feedback continuously detects and corrects data issues
cells.threshold: Automated exception detection; data-related failures falling for ≥3 cycles
cells.requirement: Automated exception detection; data-related failures falling over three or more cycles
cells.anchor: Feedback detects and corrects data issues continuously across the agreed scope.
cells.evidence: Exception detection, controlled remediation and sustained reductions in data-related failures.
cells.boundary: Automation without monitoring and recovery is insufficient.

cells.name: Ad hoc
cells.test: Isolated AI experiment with no repeatable deployment path
cells.threshold: ≥1 documented AI experiment with users and purpose
cells.requirement: At least one documented AI experiment by the retailer (selling AI devices does not count)
cells.anchor: An isolated AI experiment or manual use is confirmed without a repeatable deployment path.
cells.evidence: A documented experiment and its limited users or purpose.
cells.boundary: Do not assign Level 1 because the retailer publishes little.

cells.name: Defined
cells.test: A named initiative defines the AI workflow and delivery approach
cells.threshold: ≥1 named AI initiative with scope and partner or plan date
cells.requirement: A named AI initiative with a defined scope, partner or plan date
cells.anchor: A named initiative defines the intended AI workflow and delivery approach.
cells.evidence: A concrete project, use-case description or pilot announcement.
cells.boundary: Future benefit estimates are not measured outcomes.

cells.name: Operational
cells.test: An AI workflow operates in a stated customer or colleague setting
cells.threshold: ≥1 AI workflow live in the stated market (observed or primary-source statement)
cells.requirement: At least one AI workflow live in a stated customer or colleague setting
cells.anchor: An AI workflow operates in a stated customer or colleague setting.
cells.evidence: Current deployment evidence or a clear published statement of live use, pending validation.
cells.boundary: A demonstration alone does not establish routine production use.

cells.name: Managed
cells.test: Adoption and performance are managed across an expanded scope
cells.threshold: ≥2 live workflows with usage, monitoring and incident data over ≥2 cycles
cells.requirement: Two or more live workflows with usage, monitoring and incident data over two or more cycles
cells.anchor: The retailer manages adoption and performance across an expanded scope.
cells.evidence: Usage, monitoring, incident handling and repeated outcome reviews with a responsible owner.
cells.boundary: One reported outcome or an unnamed group-wide rollout is insufficient.

cells.name: Adaptive
cells.test: Governed AI workflows adapt and coordinate with sustained value
cells.threshold: ≥3 governed workflows; change control; sustained outcomes
cells.requirement: Three or more governed workflows with change control and sustained outcomes
cells.anchor: Governed AI workflows adapt and coordinate with sustained value across the agreed scope.
cells.evidence: Change controls, feedback-driven improvements and durable outcomes across several workflows.
cells.boundary: Autonomy is not inherently more mature than a well-controlled assistant.

cells.name: Ad hoc
cells.test: A named sponsor supports an AI activity, and at least one AI result is reported, even anecdotally
cells.threshold: Named local sponsor or expert for ≥1 AI activity; ≥1 AI use case with an ad hoc reported result
cells.requirement: Named local sponsor or expert for ≥1 AI activity; ≥1 AI use case with an ad hoc reported result
cells.anchor: Operating model: A local sponsor or informal expert supports a confirmed activity. Measurement: A confirmed use case relies on anecdotal or irregular reporting.
cells.evidence: Operating model: Named local responsibility and evidence of an informal process. Measurement: An example of the reporting practice and its known limitations.
cells.boundary: Lack of a public AI organization chart is not a Level 1 finding. No public KPI disclosure is Unknown, not Level 1.

cells.name: Defined
cells.test: An identifiable AI owner, partner or training programme exists, and a defined AI indicator is reported
cells.threshold: Named AI owner, delivery partner or defined training programme; ≥1 AI metric with defined numerator and period
cells.requirement: Named AI owner, delivery partner or defined training programme; ≥1 AI metric with defined numerator and period
cells.anchor: Operating model: An identifiable owner, partner arrangement or structured training program supports the initiative. Measurement: The retailer reports a defined AI activity, adoption or discovery indicator.
cells.evidence: Operating model: Named responsibilities, a delivery relationship or a defined training program. Measurement: A traceable metric with a stated activity and period; missing definitions remain explicit.
cells.boundary: A single training count does not prove proficiency or current coverage. AI-PC sales share measures a product category, not internal AI effectiveness.

cells.name: Operational
cells.test: Repeatable roles, prioritisation and training operate, and a use-case outcome is measured in a stated scope
cells.threshold: Decision rights and delivery cadence documented; role-based training running; ≥1 use-case outcome with numerator, denominator and scope
cells.requirement: Decision rights and delivery cadence documented; role-based training running; ≥1 use-case outcome with numerator, denominator and scope
cells.anchor: Operating model: Repeatable roles, prioritization and training processes operate across the assessed scope. Measurement: The retailer measures a use-case outcome within a stated operational scope.
cells.evidence: Operating model: Decision rights, a delivery cadence and evidence of role-based training or adoption reviews. Measurement: An outcome such as issue resolution, time saved or conversion with an identifiable use case.
cells.boundary: A senior appointment alone does not establish an operating model. A single outcome supports provisional Level 3, not causal incrementality.

cells.name: Managed
cells.test: Capacity and proficiency are managed against priorities, and interventions are linked to outcomes with valid comparisons
cells.threshold: Proficiency reviewed against priorities over ≥2 cycles; baseline + comparison group reviewed over ≥2 cycles
cells.requirement: Proficiency reviewed against priorities over ≥2 cycles; baseline + comparison group reviewed over ≥2 cycles
cells.anchor: Operating model: The organization manages capacity and proficiency against business priorities. Measurement: A regular measurement process links interventions to business outcomes using valid comparisons.
cells.evidence: Operating model: Skills measures, portfolio decisions, accountability and operating reviews across multiple cycles. Measurement: Baselines, denominators, comparison design and review records across at least two cycles.
cells.boundary: Headcount and course completion alone are insufficient. Before-and-after movement without confounder controls is insufficient.

cells.name: Adaptive
cells.test: Resources and standards are updated from learning, and measurement guides investment with sustained incremental value
cells.threshold: Documented resourcing or standards changes from reviews; replicated effect incl. cost & return; a changed investment decision
cells.requirement: Documented resourcing or standards changes from reviews; replicated effect incl. cost & return; a changed investment decision
cells.anchor: Operating model: The operating model reallocates resources and updates skills through demonstrated learning. Measurement: Continuous measurement guides investment and verifies sustained incremental value.
cells.evidence: Operating model: Documented changes to resourcing or standards and sustained improvement in delivery outcomes. Measurement: Replicated effects, cost and return treatment, and evidence that findings change investment decisions.
cells.boundary: A center of excellence label does not establish this level. Vendor benchmarks cannot substitute for retailer evidence.

scoring.rule: Each level has a test. Work up from Level 1 and stop at the first level not met — that is the score. A strong signal at a higher level cannot make up for a missing one below it. If Level 1 is not met, the dimension is recorded as Not established rather than zero.
scoring.labels: The integer is the highest level met in sequence; the decimals show progress toward the next level (its weighted evidence ÷ the level threshold, capped at .99; .00 when the next level has no questions). H marks key evidence older than 12 months. Example: L1.40 H = Level 1 met, 40% of the way to Level 2, on evidence older than 12 months.
scoring.excluded: Check pending, N/A and competitive (vendor or retailer) questions are left out of the denominator.
scoring.inference: A live Level 3 workflow implies the Level 1 and 2 anchors, so by default an untested lower level is inferred from the tested level above it. Untested top levels are never inferred: they are the ceiling.

readme.v: The final question set, built from three independent reworkings of the original 229: the C5i v2 shortlist, Rajasekar's set and Mayank's set. Where all three agreed, the decision stood. Where they differed, the deciding rule was whether an agent can retrieve the answer from a public source on a monthly cycle.
OEM axis: how [VENDOR] products are treated against [COMPETING VENDORS] inside this retailer. Retailer axis: how this retailer performs against [PEER RETAILERS].
They are reported alongside the maturity score, never added to it, so scores stay comparable across retailers and markets.
Every question carries a retrieval method, an evidence type, an answer type and a cadence. Anything that would require an interview, an internal document or a judgement call has been removed.

stop_reasons.D1: Level 3 is the ceiling of the 158-question set for D1: no public-source maturity question sits at Level 4 or 5. Under the 229-question set, Level 4 needed repeat visibility and accuracy audits with a named owner, which Best Buy does not publish.
stop_reasons.D2: Level 3 is the ceiling for D2. Level 4 (owned data-quality KPIs and an incident log) is not tested by any public-source question.
stop_reasons.D3: Level 3 is the ceiling for D3. Level 1 has no question and is inferred from the live Level 3 workflows (agentic checkout, support assistant, Ask Blue).
stop_reasons.D4: Level 4 needs AI capacity managed against priorities and outcomes tested against a comparison. The two Level 4 questions score 25%: AI-specific funding is not disclosed (D4-10) and no comparison-group result is published (D4-20).

evidence_states.name: Fetched

evidence_states.name: Accepted
evidence_states.description: Validated against the rubric, level spec and evidence rules; counts toward the cell.

evidence_states.name: Adjudication
evidence_states.description: Conflicting claims kept side by side until a reviewer decides. The affected level stays unresolved.

evidence_states.name: Needs refresh
evidence_states.description: Dynamic evidence past its freshness window; re-capture before publication.

evidence_states.name: Unknown
evidence_states.description: Not enough evidence to decide, for example a sample that is too small.

evidence_states.name: Revalidate
evidence_states.description: Older than 12 months; find current evidence or keep it marked H.
